tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session

Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).

MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.

Obligations (all mandatory):
1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. No verdict changes on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft].

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states this is the only reason outside DS-v1's list
(`rewind_ok_iff`, R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so `rewind` is `ok` whenever the
mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. **Exact outcome, proved** (`rewind_ok_iff`, hypothesis: the state
  invariant `DReach` only, no `KInv`, no I3): for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` iff `m` is
  live for the stack (DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from
  `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model does not check the DS-v1 condition
  explicitly. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, effective
  mode of §43; §61.3 follows). No other check of `split` or `release` rejects on such a state:
  - `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`: §76.2 and §76.3 at
    `newStack`, kept by every step since modes and footprints never change, §42);
  - every anchor names an existing authority (`dBound_of_reachable`), so the fresh authority
    anchors no place (§62.3, §62.4).

  The only rejection outside DS-v1's list is §36 (DS-R12). Not proved here: whether the explicit
  §36 check ever rejects when the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at
  `Modify`) would accept.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F

import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
import Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement

/-!
# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v1, non-normative)

A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. The spec does not define
its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
contract **DS-v1**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v1 item
says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
administrations) and §58 (outcomes).

DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived
from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes `m`
and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its
static checks, the availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow`
is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise).

Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

/-! ## Library state (DS-v1; §38, §46, §47) -/

/-- A block issued by a stack (DS-v1, non-normative; recorded like the issuances of §46): position
`base` of its first cell and number `size` of cells among the ordered cells of the stack, block
authority `auth`, destination `dst` that received it. -/
structure Blk where
  base : Nat
  size : Nat
  auth : Nat
  dst : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A mark (DS-v1, non-normative: "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
library metadata of an administrative abstraction, §36, §38): the identity of its stack, its fresh
identifier, the top of the stack when it was taken. -/
structure Mark where
  stack : Nat
  id : Nat
  top : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A stack (DS-v1, non-normative; library state, §38, §46): administered storage, `internal`
authority held by the stack value (§36), ordered cells (the leaves of the storage at creation),
top (the cells at positions `≥ top` are available), issued blocks (oldest first), and the ordered
list of live marks (DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks"). -/
structure Stack where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  cells : List Nat
  top : Nat
  blocks : List Blk
  marks : List Mark
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- State of the stack library (DS-v1, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
structure DState where
  kern : S3
  stacks : List Stack
  fresh : Nat

/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v1,
non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩

/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v1,
non-normative). -/
def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n

/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v1, non-normative, "a cell above m"; reading recorded; §46
available leaves): the positions from the top of `m` to the current top, those that `rewind m`
returns to available. -/
def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)

/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v1, non-normative): storage,
`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩

/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v1, non-normative). -/
def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)

/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v1, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): it names stack `j` and belongs to its list of live
marks. -/
def LiveMark (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop := m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks

/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v1). -/
instance (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark j st m) := by
  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance

/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v1, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
value, the place holding `internal`. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v1). -/
instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/

/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v1, non-normative): the
`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 read for a stack), and the guard of §56
over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, read for a stack (DS-v1). -/
  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v1). -/
instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `newStack` (DS-v1, non-normative; §36: registration adds no rights): a stack whose
cells are the leaves of the storage, top 0, no block, no mark; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
def newStackEff (D : DState) (storage internal : Nat) : DState :=
  { D with stacks := D.stacks ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint D.kern.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }

/-- `newStack` as a relation (DS-v1, non-normative; §56, §58): `ok` or `reject`. -/
def NewStackStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (D : DState) :
    Outcome3 DState → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks others storage internal) (newStackEff D storage internal)

/-! ## `push` (DS-v1: the derived `issue`, Part XIV, §77) -/

/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }

/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v1, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; reading recorded),
then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
`dst` (O8). -/
inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
      ¬ st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length → PushStep k j size dst D .fail
  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern .reject →
      PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | store {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      PushStep k j size dst D
        (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩)

/-! ## `mark` (DS-v1) -/

/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v1, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }

/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §58 outcomes; §36: metadata only, no right created): `ok`
on an existing stack; the identifier is fresh. -/
inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)

/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v1) -/

/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
  { st with
    top := m.top
    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }

/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v1, non-normative): `fail`, the state unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark;
`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
above `m` (reading recorded): `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active
authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release`
of the derived authority (O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are
removed. -/
inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark j st m → RewindStep k j m D .fail
  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st →
      RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → AdminRight D.kern st →
      SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | release {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      RewindStep k j m D (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩)

/-! ## `grow` (DS-v1: in place, the derived `issue`) -/

/-- In-place extension (DS-v1, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): the block ends at the top, and
`extra` available cells follow it. -/
def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
  x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length

/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v1). -/
instance (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Decidable (InPlace st x extra) := by
  unfold InPlace; infer_instance

/-- The grown block (DS-v1, non-normative: same base, `extra` more cells, new authority `a`, same
destination; an issuance of §46). -/
def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, x.dst⟩

/-- Metadata after `grow` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with
    top := st.top + extra
    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a else y }

/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v1, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
when `b` is not a block of the stack or `extra` is zero (reading recorded); `release` of `b` (O3);
then the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size
`size + extra` into the recorded destination, on the released state: its static checks
(`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state unchanged, unless the extension is in place
(DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split` of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new
block (O8). -/
inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noExtra {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → extra = 0 →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → 0 < extra →
      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
      ¬ InPlace st x extra → GrowStep k j b extra D .fail
  | split {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | store {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ (.ok s₃) →
      GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok ⟨s₃, D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra s₁.A.length), D.fresh⟩)

/-! ## Library runs (DS-v1; §36, §56, §57) -/

/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v1, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'

/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v1, non-normative; §47). -/
inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'

/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v1, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''

/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
`split` then `release`; DS-v1). -/
theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hk => exact .step hr hk
  | newStack hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hr
  | push hs =>
    cases hs with
    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ => exact hr

content.content:
## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

-----
## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

-----
## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
-----

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation is installed on the relevant leaves. While it is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone(place)` attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The corresponding dynamic pinning obligation ends, without itself modifying values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.
